name: US EIA Electric Power Annual Table 2.3 - Revenue from Sales of Electricity to Ultimate Customers by Sector
notes: Government primary source, numerator half of the derived US electricity price. Table 2.3 'Revenue from Sales of Electricity to Ultimate Customers by Sector, by Provider, 2014 through 2024 (Million Dollars)'. Values used, Total Electric Industry row: 2024 total 514,396 M USD, commercial 185,043, industrial 84,095, residential 244,367. 2023 total 491,370. 2022 total 485,249. DERIVATION, shown so it can be re-checked: cents per kWh = (revenue_MUSD * 1e6 USD / (volume_MWh * 1000 kWh/MWh)) / 10. For 2024 all-sector this gives 514,396e6 / 3,975,381,832 kWh = 0.12940 USD/kWh = 12.94 cents/kWh; commercial 185,043e6 / 1,450,941,216 = 12.75 cents/kWh; industrial 84,095e6 / 1,034,584,190 = 8.13 cents/kWh. IMPORTANT SCOPE CAVEAT, stated in the supply record: these are AVERAGE RETAIL prices to ultimate customers across all US states, including any residential or small-commercial volume in the average. They are not a data-centre tariff. A real hyperscale load is bought at industrial or wholesale rates, frequently in a specific state with its own rate design, and often under a contract that prices capacity separately from energy. Treat 12.94 cents/kWh as a US-average reference point, not as a quote.
